chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Zayd Al Narsy, from Ali Bin Mazeyd a companion of Al Sabiri who said:

I went over to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I took his hand and I kissed it. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'But it is not correct except for a Prophet (peace be upon him) or a successor (peace be upon him) of a Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)'.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on kissing the hand of an Imam or Prophet in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the narrator kisses the hand of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who clarifies that such an act of profound submission is reserved exclusively for a Prophet or his designated successor (Wasi). This narration underscores the unique spiritual status of the Imams as inheritors of prophetic authority, distinguishing their rank from that of ordinary believers while affirming the legitimacy of showing reverence to them. It highlights the Shia concept of *Wilayah*, where the Imam’s hand is kissed not merely as a cultural gesture but as an acknowledgment of divine appointment.
